text:
maya: heads-up — saw an incident where interleaved IO for small-shard workloads starved a sequential streaming job. digging into warmup priorities now.

devin: ugh. is this the case where prefix cache fills with many tiny shard reads and the streaming read waits behind their IO queue? :grimacing:

maya: yep. streaming model was trying to pull an entire layer sequentially but the IO scheduler had a lot of tiny ranges from concurrent requests. throughput for the sequential reader dropped ~4x.

raj: is this at the OS scheduler level or our transport level? could we bias the read queue per-request?

maya: looks like a mix. kernel I/O reordering + our transfer worker pool. the transport conflates all reads into a single priority class right now.

sasha: quick Q: do we want strict priority (streaming always wins) or weighted fairness (streaming gets higher share but not starve small reads)?

devin: weighted fairness is safer for multi-tenant; strict priority could kill latency for interactive tails. but fairness needs a simple, auditable policy.

maya: prototype idea: read tickets with two dimensions — weight and deadline. streaming requests get higher weight and a deadline based on observed seq throughput (shorter deadlines). small requests get lower weight but earlier soft deadlines. scheduler picks by max(weight / age) or similar.

raj: sounds like WFQ-ish. we should avoid complex global state. can we express as a token-bucket per-class + per-shard hint?

maya: yeah — per-priority token buckets are simpler. plus we can add a per-shard hint header: `x-warmup-priority: streaming|interactive|background` and `x-warmup-weight: <0-100>`. transports can fast-path streaming hints into contiguous reads.

infra-bot: deploy-log: canary rollout of transport v2 started for region us-west-2 by sasha at 2026-03-21T15:02:00Z

sasha: note — need backward compat with older checkpointers that don't emit hints. fallback should guess streaming when request has `range: full-layer` pattern.

devin: another tradeoff — fairer policies increase head latency for streaming during peak. do we want an opt-in override for Dedicated customers to enforce strict streaming SLO?

maya: yes: config knobs per-deployment: `streaming_slo_enforcement: none|soft|hard`. soft = weighted fairness favor streaming but allow others; hard = streaming wins preemptively.

raj: can we quantify cost? maybe simulate with traces. i'll run a batch of 1k mixed-workload traces and measure 95th pct for both classes under soft vs hard.

maya: appreciated. also adding simple telemetry: per-request `warmup_wait_ms`, `read_merge_hits`, `priority_class` so we can correlate.

devin: implementation notes: transport should expose a `ReadHint` proto field. runtime layer uses it to decide chunking and whether to submit large contiguous reads vs many small ones.

maya: pseudo-config for ops: ```
# warmup scheduling
priority_classes:
  - name: streaming
    weight: 80
    token_rate: 2000 # bytes/sec per-worker
  - name: interactive
    weight: 15
    token_rate: 500
  - name: background
    weight: 5
    token_rate: 200
streaming_slo_enforcement: soft
```

sasha: god idea to keep token_rate bytes/sec; maps to admission for NVMe queue depth. ops can tune per-instance.

raj: testing plan: 1) single-node replay; 2) canary in us-west with mixed traffic; 3) enable telemetry and dashboards (per-route) before global rollout.

maya: blockers: need small API change for `ReadHint` and a tiny transport codec bump; also need a short RFC to document `streaming_slo_enforcement` semantics.

devin: i can take the RFC (short). raj takes simulation and dashboards. sasha will own canary. maya will PR transport changes.

sasha: fyi — if we go with token buckets, add an escape hatch to disable hint parsing entirely for Private installs (compliance teams asked).

maya: noted. i'll add that to the RFC.

raj: one final thought — prefer additive backoff for weights when storage is overloaded rather than hard cutoff. we want graceful degradation not service denial.

maya: agreed. that'll be in the proposal. thanks all :+1:
